findings.text: §4's done-when asserts "a stranded request of a lost session is retired with §5's reason and is absent from the decision", but `plan-section-depends-on` lists only `s2` for `s4`, so a §4 node dispatched beside §5 fails its own gate on a behaviour §5 owns, and §5's own done-when carries no lost-session case

findings.reason: the deliverable has no measure and no owner, which is the defect §8 was reshaped to remove one finding earlier, and here it also strands a write into a spliced evidence record.
findings.text: §12's first deliverable is "an inventory in the plan's landed record of every place in `reckon/` that decides behaviour from a backend's name or from a harness dialect", and the done-when at :131 asserts only the composed-worker equality test, so a worker can pass the gate with no inventory written, in a cumulative archive file the node does not own

findings.reason: one verdict cannot close a survey and a normalisation, so the section is either closed with the inventory unwritten or held open by a behaviour change the survey no longer describes; splitting them is the repair already applied to §6.
findings.text: §12 explicitly delivers "two things": an inventory document and the removal of every incidental difference in worker behaviour across the harnesses, a document and a cross-tree behaviour change with two different gates

findings.reason: only the gate-hold case is pinned by a negative control, so the section's stated endpoint, that what a worker is given does not depend on its harness, is unchecked for every other dimension.
findings.text: the equality test is told to assert sameness "differing only in the fields the inventory lists as forced", but nothing cross-checks the forced/incidental split and the inventory carries no measure, so one field declared forced (inbox delivery, say) drops it from the comparison and the gate passes with the behaviour still differing

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §14 cites its three pointers with one run id truncated by an ellipsis, so that record cannot be opened; elsewhere the cited head, the research directory, `audit-doc` and §12's gate-hold comparison all resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §12's first deliverable, an inventory in the plan's landed record, is measured by nothing in its done-when.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every new section's evidence is a test file in the repository plus the run's own record, and §12's inventory lands in `docs/evidence/archive/`; no section names a session scratchpad or a node-local path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the named tests, settings and sections carry no plan labels, ticket numbers, version tags or changelog prose, and the dated incident narrative sits in plan prose rather than in a symbol or comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §12's equality measure is parameterised by the same unmeasured inventory it is meant to prove, so every dimension except the gate hold may be declared forced and skipped, and the gate passes with no behaviour made the same.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §12 names two deliverables, an inventory document and a cross-tree removal of incidental differences, and one verdict cannot close both.
